children: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be in Chennai on Sunday October 11 for a series of events including the flag off of a new section of the Chennai Metro and inauguration of projects.

As per an official government statement, at around  11.30 am, he will undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back. He will likely be joined by TN CM Joseph Vijay for this ride. He will also inaugurate the new Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around ₹4,900 crore.
Then, he will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple in Chennai. Thereafter, he will take a walkthrough of the Brain Centre at IIT Madras.

This will be followed by the Prime Minister laying the foundation stone , inaugurating and dedicating various development projects worth over ₹13,000 crore. He will also address the gathering at this occasion.
Finally, the PM will also participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai.
He will lay the foundation stone of and inaugurate key National Highway projects worth around ₹3,700 crore.
Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over ₹750 crore.

He will also inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of several port-related projects in Tamil Nadu to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency. This includes four infrastructure projects at Chennai Port: a Paved Storage Yard, four EXIM Godowns, an upgraded Cruise Terminal and a Seafarers Club.

Further, PM Modi will lay the foundation stone of the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd (CPCL) in Chennai. With a total cost of around ₹1,620 crore and a capacity of 270 thousand  tonnes per annum , the project aims to produce Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks for the manufacture of world-class, premium-quality lubricants in India.

At the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre (SGBC) at IIT Madras, he is also set to launch its pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan — from the foetal stage to old age.

title: PM Narendra Modi in Chennai on Sunday for a series of engagements
